status: Four proposed Belize finding-aid connections for existing directory entries; no canonical research-status changes

associations.name: Garifuna
associations.associationType: Living community and community-representation connection in national cultural reporting
associations.sourceTitle: Capacity Building Project of the Living African-descendant Heritage in the SICA Region and Cuba — NICH
associations.sourceType: Primary national cultural-institute project account, written by April Martinez, NICH-ISCR
associations.evidenceNote: NICH identifies Garifuna communities as part of Belize's living heritage and names a National Garifuna Council representative on its Belize project team. This supports a present-day Belize community connection, rather than reducing Garifuna identity to an earlier Caribbean migration history or treating Garifuna and Kriol as interchangeable.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML article dated October 22, 2024: Belize national team and Garifuna Council representative, lines 33–47; safeguarding approach, lines 52–62; author credit, lines 63–65. Related NICH 2024–25 fund entry explicitly describes a Garifuna-language resource for learners in Belize. No restricted practice or cultural instruction reproduced.
limits: Country connection only; the source does not enumerate every Garifuna settlement or define a territorial polygon.
A 2024 named project representative is not asserted to hold the same office in October 2026.
Garifuna and Kriol remain distinct named communities in the source.

associations.name: Mopan Maya
associations.associationType: Present cultural-community connection in a national grant record
associations.period: Belize Culture Fund grant cycles 2023–24 and 2024–25
associations.sourceTitle: Belize Culture Fund Awardees — National Institute of Culture and History
associations.evidenceNote: NICH describes Katherine Karas's Mopan Maya photographic project through her family roots in southern Belize and lists a later Mopan mentor-and-apprentice initiative. These are living cultural-community connections. They do not assign every archaeological Maya site in Belize to Mopan people.
associations.reviewedScope: Actual HTML fund administration and grant-cycle headings; Katherine Karas entry, lines 128–131; Stanley Peck mentorship entry, lines 159–162. No project completion or current funding is inferred.
limits: Family and cultural-program accounts do not represent all Mopan histories or priorities. Broad country geography only; no archaeological identity or boundary inferred.

associations.name: Q'eqchi'
associations.associationType: Contemporary linguistic-community geography in community-coauthored scholarship
associations.period: Work published online August 8, 2025; geographic passage inspected October 21, 2026
associations.sourceTitle: Defending Community, Territory, and Indigenous Environmental Relations — Levi Gahman, Filiberto Penados, Cristina Coc and Shelda-Jane Smith
associations.sourceType: Original open-access research coauthored by a Maya Leaders Alliance representative
associations.evidenceNote: The authors identify Q'eqchi' and Mopan as distinct linguistic communities living predominantly in southern Belize. This is a present-community connection, rather than an inference from archaeological remains.
associations.reviewedScope: Publisher HTML, Section 2 geographic introduction, lines 641–643; author affiliations and August 8, 2025 publication date also checked.
limits: Selected geography only; no present population total, land boundary or legal holding adopted.

associations.name: Maya
associations.associationType: Broader Maya access point overlapping specifically named contemporary communities
associations.period: Contemporary community geography in scholarship published August 8, 2025
associations.sourceTitle: Defending Community, Territory, and Indigenous Environmental Relations — community-coauthored Cambridge Element
associations.sourceType: Original open-access research coauthored by a Maya Leaders Alliance representative
associations.evidenceNote: The same passage names multiple Maya linguistic groups in Belize. This broader access point overlaps the Mopan and Q'eqchi' entries, rather than denoting an additional distinct nation.
associations.reviewedScope: Section 2 opening geographic paragraph; NICH contemporary cultural-project pages separately checked.
limits: Maya is an umbrella; no archaeological site is assigned a modern language identity.

educationalContext.title: Living Maya communities
educationalContext.text: These routes concern living Maya communities. The broad Maya entry overlaps specifically named peoples and should not assign their identities to every archaeological site.

educationalContext.title: Heritage work today
educationalContext.text: The national cultural institute's reports document Mopan mentorship, family photography and Garifuna-language learning. Such projects offer specific ways into contemporary cultural life; a grant entry gives a project's reported scope, rather than a complete account of a people.

educationalContext.title: Garifuna and distinct community voices
educationalContext.text: The 2024 heritage account names Garifuna and Kriol representatives separately. Its collaborative approach supplies useful context for following community organizations while retaining their distinct identities.

excludedOrSupportingInspections.title: New Julian Cho Society / Maya of Southern Belize website

excludedOrSupportingInspections.decision: Excluded from proposed association evidence pending confirmation of current organizational authorization and finished editorial content. No present program outputs or population figures adopted.
Blocked by a JavaScript/human-verification page. No challenge bypassed, and no uninspected UNESCO content used.

unresolved.name: Itza Maya
unresolved.reason: The inspected selection did not establish a specific historical or contemporary Itza Maya community connection in Belize. Broad Maya presence, nearby Petén communities, place names and archaeological affiliations do not suffice to add this route.
unresolved.nextResearchNeed: A directly relevant community publication, primary historical account or specialist study explicitly locating Itza people in Belize, with a clear period and careful distinction from Mopan, Yucatec and generic archaeological Maya.

Historical migrations and archaeological language affiliations were not established in this bounded pass.
